Orchard is the first word in the recording and the team is meeting to review the migration plan. We will start with the Postgres database and check whether the Kubernetes deployment can roll back safely. The OpenTelemetry collector forwards traces while Redis absorbs bursts from the busiest parts of the service. On Tuesday the team will review a long list of alerts and separate noisy signals from the important ones. The build should use Bazel to produce the same artifacts on a laptop and on the continuous integration workers. We can keep the old connection open while the new connection has enough time to confirm the handoff. An engineer will check each dashboard and write down the results before anyone moves another part of the system. The security review covers WebAssembly and asks how much memory it needs when several documents are open. We will copy the incident timeline into a shared document so that the support team can answer customer questions. The test needs to cover a weak connection and a restart while a user is still working on a message. When the logs are ready we will compare the names in the report with the names in the release notes. At the end of the week we will read the entire report from beginning to end and say the final word lighthouse.
